concerns.text: T200 mandates querying external repositories (NCBI SRA, EGA) for real data. This violates Constitution Principle I (Reproducibility) which requires 'External datasets MUST be fetched from the same canonical source on every run.' Network-dependent discovery is non-deterministic and cannot be reproduced on a fresh runner without manual intervention, effectively weakening the FR-007 execution constraint.

T021f_fetch requires fetching an external 'NCBI taxonomy dump' to identify definitionally related pairs for FR-006 (Collinearity). This introduces a non-deterministic dependency (network fetch, version drift) for a core statistical requirement. If the fetch fails or taxonomy versions differ, the system cannot guarantee the 'Perfect Multicollinearity' detection required by the spec, violating Constitution Principle I.

T201 implements a warning for N < 30 but does not enforce the 'Underpowered' flag required by SC-005 and FR-002 logic. The task description says 'Do not halt, but flag', whereas the spec requires the system to 'flag the study as Underpowered' as a mandatory outcome of the power analysis, not just a warning. This is a semantic weakening of the acceptance criteria.

T022 enforces a hard switch to SparCC/SpiecEasi if compositionality is detected. The spec's Edge Cases state the system 'SHOULD use SparCC or SpiecEasi if available'. The task removes the 'if available' fallback, creating a brittle pipeline that will fail on standard CI runners if these heavy dependencies are missing, violating the 'Compute Feasibility' and 'Reproducibility' constraints of the plan.

T300 allows execution on 'synthetic data' if no real data is found, flagging it as 'SYNTHETIC VALIDATION ONLY'. However, SC-005 requires measuring statistical power against a minimum sample size for the *study*. Synthetic data (T107) cannot validly demonstrate the power of a real-world biological hypothesis. This task silently relaxes the requirement to validate the study's power on actual data, rendering SC-005 untestable in the fallback path.
